Tabulate centrality stability results

Source: R/methods-stability.R
as.data.frame.htna_stability.Rd

as.data.frame() returns the results of centrality_stability_htna() as a tidy data frame; summary() of a grouped result returns the stacked correlation table. The CS coefficients (one row per measure) summarize how many sessions can be dropped before the centrality ranking changes; the correlation table (one row per measure and drop proportion) shows the trace behind each coefficient. For a grouped result the rows of every cohort are stacked with a leading group column.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'htna_stability'
as.data.frame(
  x,
  row.names = NULL,
  optional = FALSE,
  ...,
  what = c("cs", "correlations")
)

# S3 method for class 'htna_stability_group'
as.data.frame(
  x,
  row.names = NULL,
  optional = FALSE,
  ...,
  what = c("cs", "correlations")
)

# S3 method for class 'htna_stability_group'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

x

An htna_stability or htna_stability_group.

row.names, optional

Ignored; present for the generic.

...

Unused.

what

"cs" (default) for the CS coefficients, or "correlations" for the correlation table.

object

An htna_stability_group.

Value

A data frame. For what = "cs": columns measure and cs, one row per measure. For what = "correlations": columns measure, drop_prop, mean_cor, sd_cor and prop_above (the share of resamples with a correlation above the threshold), one row per measure and drop proportion. Grouped results add a first column group. summary() of a grouped result returns the stacked correlation table.

See also

centrality_stability_htna(), plot.htna_stability()

Examples

data(human_ai)
net <- build_htna(human_ai, actor_type = "actor_type")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (42 sessions), 'actor_type' (24 sessions)
cs  <- centrality_stability_htna(net, iter = 20, seed = 1)
as.data.frame(cs)
#>       measure  cs
#> 1  InStrength 0.9
#> 2 OutStrength 0.9
#> 3 Betweenness 0.9
as.data.frame(cs, what = "correlations")
